title: Sylvan Health — initial prospect scouting notes
body:
Quick brain dump on Sylvan Health (regional payer and value-based care org) — tidy later. Purpose: scout fit + craft 3-email sequence + call script + known objections.

Account snapshot:
- HQ: Minneapolis, mid-sized payer (~2.5k employees), operates both commercial and Medicare Advantage plans.
- Recent public initiatives: announced care coordination platform (Q2 2025), looking to modernize member engagement, listed investments in predictive care ops.
- Tech signals: job posts for data platform engineers, ML infra, and a cloud modernization RFP (Dec 2024).
- Likely constraints: HIPAA/regulatory focus, procurement cycles, preference for VPC/KMS, conservative infra ops.

Why Redwood could matter (top-level value props to test):
1) Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) + KMS/HSM integration — lowers legal/security friction.
2) Predictable latency and batching controls — relevant for member-facing chat and real-time telephony flows.
3) Cost-aware tooling (Optimize) — helpful to justify unit economics for high-volume outreach and embeddings.
4) Built-in rollouts/fallbacks — reduces risk for pilot (can canary smaller cohorts to MSISDN or plan IDs).

Target use cases to pitch initially:
- Member engagement assistant: triage inbound calls and route to nurse line with automated briefings (short generation, structured outputs).
- Claims triage & auto-summary: reduce time for claims analysts by surfacing key claim facts + precedent language.
- Personalized outreach at scale: generate short, compliant messages for care plans with audit logs.

Stakeholder map (hypothesis — validate):
- Dir of Digital Experience (primary champion) — cares about member experience/KPIs (NPS, containment).
- Head of Data/ML Platforms — procurement gate for infra choices.
- Security/compliance lead — will require SOC2/HIPAA docs, KMS proof, audit logs.
- Procurement + Legal — long cycle, will negotiate data residency and indemnity.

Potential pilot metrics that resonate:
- Reduce average handling time (AHT) for triage by X% (targets: 20–35%).
- Increase member self-serve containment rate by Y pp (targets: +8–12 pp).
- Token cost per member contact < $0.02 for templated flows (use Redwood Optimize recommendations).
- Time-to-value: pilot in 6–8 weeks with dedicated capacity.

Objections we will see + suggested responses:
- "We can't send PHI to a third party": offer private deployment (customer-managed VPC), KMS integration, contract language and on-prem option. Provide redacted architecture diagram and SOC2/HIPAA checklist.
- "Model hallucination risk for clinical guidance": emphasize guardrails — function/tool calling + structured output templates + human-in-the-loop for high-risk intents. Propose conservative scope for pilot (status updates, scheduling, summaries) not clinical advice.
- "Cost unpredictability": show Optimize suite + batching/caching examples, run a small benchmarking exercise projecting monthly spend by volume tiers. Offer fixed-price pilot for first 3 months.
- "Integration work / engineering burden": provide lightweight SDK examples, pre-built adapters for common EHR connectors (FHIR + HL7 notes), and offer solutions-engineering hours in pilot package.

Cold outreach draft (email v1) — short and testable:
Subject: Small pilot to reduce member triage time at Sylvan Health
Hi [First],
I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference — we help health plans run LLMs behind their VPCs so member-facing assistants and claims summarization run with audit logs and predictable cost.
Would you be open to a 20-minute pilot plan review? We can map a 6-week pilot that protects PHI, shows AHT impact, and hands off a reproducible infra pattern to your platform team.
Best,
Jordan

Follow-up / LinkedIn note (brief):
Spoke to [XX] at [event]? Would love 10–15 min to share a quick case study on a MA plan that cut call center handle time using a private LLM pilot.

Call opener bullets (1–2 min):
- Thank you, confirm agenda: 1) quick pain check, 2) pilot approach, 3) next steps.
- Quick hypothesis: member triage + claim summaries are high ROI; can we confirm who owns these metrics?
- Ask about current infra: on-prem vs cloud, KMS, vendor restrictions.

Internal asks / assets to prepare before outreach:
- HIPAA + SOC2 one-pager tailored for payers (security team).
- A short benchmarking matrix (tokens vs latency vs cost) for two model families with private deployment numbers.
- Solutions-engineering commitment: 2x SE weeks for first pilot + template FHIR adapter.
- Case study: anonymized example of plan X that reduced AHT (if not available, create synthetic pilot numbers and label them as estimates).

Open questions / validation items:
- Who is the Dir of Digital Experience? LinkedIn search shows a "Rachel Meyers" title — need confirm.
- Procurement lead timeline: do they consolidate vendor review quarterly?
- Are there existing contracts with big cloud vendors that would complicate private deployment?
- Any preferred vendors for EHR/FHIR connectors?

Next steps (this week):
- Asha to run profile on Rachel Meyers + org chart (due: 2025-11-05).
- Liam to draft the pilot SOW sketch + baseline pricing (due: 2025-11-07).
- I (Jordan) to send the first outreach email to Rachel + cc head of data if available (send on 2025-11-06).

Scratch notes / voice-of-customer fragments to fold into later PRD:
- "We need everything audited and revertible—can't have free-text writes in member record."
- "If it saves even one RN FTE per 10k members, it's worth tooling up."
- "We won't accept model outputs that are directly used for clinical decisioning without human sign-off."

Rough timeline for pilot (proposal):
- Week 0–1: scoping call + compliance checklist signoff + network setup
- Week 2–3: integration and baseline data ingestion (de-identified or edge proxy)
- Week 4–6: run pilot on small cohort, collect AHT and containment metrics
- Week 7: results review + rollout plan or pause decision

End of dump. Keep this private — prepping a cleaner one-pager for legal/security next.
